title: NIST: standard atomic weight of Sulfur (S, Z=16) is the interval [32.059,32.076]
summary: NIST prints the standard atomic weight field of Sulfur (S, Z=16) as [32.059,32.076], with the isotope rows in the same file.
body: PubChem's periodic-table row names atomic number 16, symbol S, as Sulfur. The NIST compositions file prints the standard atomic weight of Sulfur as the interval [32.059,32.076]. This interval is the set of atomic-weight values NIST assigns to normal materials. It is not the uncertainty of one weighing. The notes field on this element's rows is blank. Isotope rows in the same file: S-32 relative atomic mass 31.9720711744(14), isotopic composition 0.9499(26); S-33 relative atomic mass 32.9714589098(15), isotopic composition 0.0075(2); S-34 relative atomic mass 33.967867004(47), isotopic composition 0.0425(24); S-36 relative atomic mass 35.96708071(20), isotopic composition 0.0001(1). A relative atomic mass is scaled to carbon-12. An isotopic composition, when the field is not blank, is a representative mole fraction, not a new assay made for this card. The symbols for an interval, a parenthesis, a bracket, and a # mark are defined on world.chemistry.nist-atomic-weight-notation. This standard atomic weight is not the Chemistry WebBook molecular-weight field, which is a different catalog entry when one exists.
